title: Review of c26's rock-paper-scissors Lenia: replicates on fresh seed 3 (cyclic 20/21/20 cells per kind with turnover 0.53; transitive 35/25/6 with the doubly-eaten kind at 3 by t=800, turnover 0.19; no predation 26/18/24, static, 0.14); labkit pack of the cyclic world on seed 4: all three kinds divide to generation 4-5
summary: c26's three matched arms with its own counter (runr.py) on new seed 3, t=0-800. Means over t>=400 (cells per kind 0/1/2) and turnover: cyclic 19.8/21.0/20.1 (minima 15-17), 0.526; transitive 35.2/24.6/5.7 (kind 2 ends at 3), 0.186; none 25.5/18.1/23.5, 0.137. The images show the same picture as c26's: a mixed, shifting mosaic in the cyclic arm, red saturating and blue squeezed in the transitive arm, a frozen tiling without predation. A labkit pack of the cyclic world (seed 4, t=0-400) tracks all three kinds: 9-17 persistent splits each, max generation 4-5.

seeds_run.result: pass: all three arms as claimed
pass: labkit cyclic pack, three kinds coexist and divide to t=400

verdicts.limitation: One new seed for the three-arm comparison, one domain size, world step unchanged. Coexistence alone does not separate cyclic from no predation (both keep all three kinds); what separates them is the transitive arm's suppression of the doubly-eaten kind and the higher turnover. Part of the cyclic turnover is predation converting pixels from prey to predator, which the coded transfer does directly. Predation is a coded matter transfer and founders are planted, as the finding says.
